reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes an Ethereum bot with a +55% per-day headline and an easy passive-income claim, while providing step-by-step deployment instructions. It directs viewers to deposit at least 0.2 ETH into a contract address and claims that larger deposits produce larger transactions and more profit, alongside displayed controls and a reported 31% result.

citations.quote: How to Make +55%/Day With an Ethereum MEV Bot
Today I'll be teaching you step-by-step how to deploy an Ethereum trading bot I've recently developed in the Solidity language, which can make you very easy daily passive income.
Deposit funds (at least 0.2 ETH to prevent negating slippage) to your exact contract/bot address
the more you put in, the larger the transactions you would be able to sandwich and the more profit you will be able to accumulate over time.
Now you can see the four actions for our smart contract. Start enables the bot to start sniffing the mempool. Withdraw stops the bot and transfers the funds back into your wallet

opening.argument: The presentation includes material risk and uncertainty rather than a guaranteed-return promise. It explains that gas and burn fees can consume funds, recommends funding levels to avoid that problem, and expressly says results vary over time. The operational discussion also describes a mechanism involving pending transactions, gas fees, and slippage, giving viewers information to evaluate the risks for themselves. Those qualifications are inconsistent with presenting income as certain or risk-free; the headline and personal results are claims to assess, not proof that every viewer will profit.

citations.quote: If you fund the contract with 0.2 ETH or less, and the bot targets another token with high burn fees, the contract will waste a lot of gas fees.
the profits will fluctuate week to week
so that it is processed before the pending transaction, allowing us to profit from the slippage differences

rebuttal.rebuttal: The headline and income language are attention-grabbing, but they do not erase the video's concrete qualifications. The prosecution treats a minimum-funding recommendation as proof of deception, even though the description gives a stated reason: avoiding gas and burn-fee losses. The reported result is also presented as a personal example, while the speaker acknowledges that profits fluctuate. The evidence therefore supports a risky, conditional trading claim, not a guaranteed outcome.

citations.quote: the contract will waste a lot of gas fees
the profits will fluctuate week to week

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The risk language does not cure the central solicitation. The video still pairs a highly attractive daily-return headline with instructions to deploy and fund a contract, and it tells viewers that larger deposits can produce more profit. Saying profits fluctuate acknowledges variability, but does not substantiate the claimed mechanism or warn that the promoted setup may simply take deposited funds. The gas-fee discussion explains how to preserve the strategy's operation; it does not independently validate it.

citations.quote: How to Make +55%/Day With an Ethereum MEV Bot
Deposit funds (at least 0.2 ETH to prevent negating slippage)

opening.argument: The primary format is a technical, step-by-step demonstration of Solidity and decentralized-finance tooling. It shows how to create a contract file, select a compiler version, deploy through Remix, and interact with the resulting contract. The speaker explains mempool monitoring, sandwich transactions, gas fees, and withdrawal controls, while the sampled frames show code, compiler settings, deployment controls, and a contract interface. A tutorial can include the creator's own performance example without becoming a certification that the method is universally profitable.

citations.quote: Today I'll be teaching you step-by-step how to deploy an Ethereum trading bot
Under compiler, select the 0.6 point six version so that it matches our contract.
Now you can see the four actions for our smart contract.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies financial claims, but the evidence also shows substantial technical instruction. The speaker explains what the bot is doing and walks through deployment, compilation, wallet connection, and contract controls. Showing a personal demonstration of balances is not the same as guaranteeing that viewers will obtain those results. The video's observable structure is an operational tutorial whose subject happens to involve a speculative trading tool.

citations.quote: Remix is a Web3 application that allows us to develop, compile, deploy, and launch smart contracts coded in the Solidity language.
Now you can see the four actions for our smart contract.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Technical instruction is the vehicle for the promotion, not a separate neutral topic. The tutorial tells viewers to deploy the contract, fund it with Ethereum, start it, and expect passive income. The personal balance display is used as purported evidence of success, while no independent verification establishes that the displayed result came from genuine trading or that the code can deliver it. Calling the content a tutorial does not remove its direct financial inducement.

citations.quote: which can make you very easy daily passive income
the more you put in, the larger the transactions you would be able to sandwich and the more profit you will be able to accumulate over time.
So as you can see I have about 1.31 ETH which is 31% profit already

opening.argument: The material describes a software-based trading service and its operating costs, not a downline, credential-theft, or guaranteed-payout scheme. The stated mechanism is automated interaction with decentralized exchanges: the bot scans pending transactions, uses gas priority, and attempts to capture slippage differences. The instructions concern creating and operating a smart contract through Remix and MetaMask; they do not request a password, seed phrase, or account credentials. The content therefore fits an ordinary technology and trading-tool promotion, with speculative returns that remain unverified rather than an established scam mechanism.

citations.quote: This arbitrage tool scans decentralized exchange Mempools, such as Uniswap and PancakeSwap, for pending transactions.
It takes advantage of decentralized finance platforms, such as Uniswap, to sandwich transactions for arbitrage.
Remix is a Web3 application that allows us to develop, compile, deploy, and launch smart contracts coded in the Solidity language
Make sure you got the right address in there.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes that viewers are told to fund a contract, but funding capital is ordinary for a trading tool and the description identifies a purported trading mechanism. The record does not show a request for credentials, a referral chain, or a promise that deposits will be returned regardless of performance. It also does not independently establish that the contract is fraudulent. On this evidence, the safer characterization is speculative software promotion, not a proven scam.

citations.quote: and we profit off slippage differences in the transaction.
the profits will fluctuate week to week

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of credential theft or a downline is not decisive because the relevant mechanism is a funded-contract return claim. The video directs viewers to send Ethereum to the exact contract address and says the bot can generate passive income, while the claimed trading operation and displayed results are not independently established. A purported mechanism can be presented convincingly without being real; describing it as software does not show that deposited funds are protected or that the promised returns are genuine.
